newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee resumes ascent, nervously awaits NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee resumes ascent, nervously awaits NY.

text.p: Robusta coffee resumed its ascent on Friday but stayed in the slow lane as Far Eastern hedging prevented it from catching up with New York.
The market was technically due $100 higher after another meteoric rise in New York Thursday, but opened a modest $30 up and had a choppy run throughout the morning dealings.
"$100 up was a little adventurous. We thought $40 up," said one trader.
"If you're going against March which is reflecting a lot of price fixing and everything else that's pouring into the 'C' (CSCE March) contract, it's going to give give you a bum steer," he added.
Some traders explained an initial paring of gains by a concerted effort to try to give New York a lower due after it soared to a 21-month high of 180.05 cents/lb basis March on Thursday.
But others disagreed, saying the two had become two separate markets now that the arbitrage is around $1 basis March.
"It's showing more and more that this business of London giving New York a due is complete nonsense," said one.
He said the session had featured a mixed pack of trade and origin selling, followed by a spate of trade buying, lifting the May contract back up to $1,696 a tonne at midday, up $36 on the day.
Traders also cited some roaster fixing and a general picking away on the nearbys.
Volume totalled a relatively modest 2,881 lots.
Traders said New York could be prone to speculative liquidation on Friday before the long weekend marked by the President's day on Monday.
"If there is going to be profit taking, you would suggest it would be today," said one.
Technical analysts also warned of the danger of a speculative ambush, recommending players to at least take some profits after increasingly overbought conditions.
Support for London was pegged at $1,600 and $1,550.
There was no news on the Colombian strike front after Thursday's talks between union leaders and government ministers.
Elsewhere, Vietnamese farmers in the main Dak Lak province were said to be holding back Robusta supplies, waiting for higher prices.
